entities.summary: Xiang Yan (b. 300 BCE) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, active in Global. Known for his role as a military leader and commander, Xiang Yan played a significant part in shaping the course of history. He served under the Han dynasty, which marked the beginning of imperial China. Xiang Yan's military campaigns helped to consolidate the empire's borders and establish a stable government. His legacy extended beyond his own time, as he was remembered for his bravery and strategic prowess by future generations. As he once said, 'A good general is like a good general's father – he must teach his children how to be good generals.' Xiang Yan's words continue to inspire military leaders to this day, and his name is still revered in China as a symbol of military excellence.
